interactives.title: Projectile motion and air resistance
interactives.sub: Launch a ball on Earth, the Moon, Mars or Jupiter, with or without drag, hit a target and find the best angle.
interactives.note: Uniform gravity and still air; quadratic drag on a 145 g baseball (C_d = 0.47); integrated numerically.

interactives.title: Collisions on an air track
interactives.sub: Elastic, sticky and exploding gliders: momentum is always conserved, kinetic energy only sometimes.
interactives.note: One dimension, frictionless track; the coefficient of restitution sets how much kinetic energy survives.

interactives.title: Damped and driven oscillations
interactives.sub: A mass on a spring: period, damping regimes, energy exchange, resonance curves and the quality factor.
interactives.note: Linear spring and viscous damping; the motion is integrated numerically and the resonance curve is the exact steady state.

interactives.title: Pendulums: small angles to chaos
interactives.sub: The exact period against 2π√(L/g), then two double pendulums released a millionth of a radian apart.
interactives.note: Point masses on light rigid rods, no friction; the exact period is computed with the arithmetic–geometric mean.

interactives.title: Orbits and Kepler's laws
interactives.sub: Launch a planet: circles, ellipses and escape, equal areas in equal times, and T² against a³.
interactives.note: Newtonian gravity from a fixed star much heavier than the planet; symplectic integration keeps energy steady.

interactives.title: Superposition, standing waves and beats
interactives.sub: Add two waves, build standing waves on a string from its tension and mass, and hear beats between two notes.
interactives.note: Ideal lossless string and pure sine waves; standing-wave motion is slowed down so it can be seen.

interactives.title: Double slit, single slit and gratings
interactives.sub: Interference fringes inside a diffraction envelope, missing orders, and the spectra a grating makes.
interactives.note: Far-field (Fraunhofer) intensity for monochromatic light; the ripple-tank picture isn't to scale.

interactives.title: DC circuits and Kirchhoff's laws
interactives.sub: Series, parallel and mixed networks, internal resistance and maximum power, and a Wheatstone bridge to balance.
interactives.note: Solved exactly by nodal analysis; ideal wires and fixed resistances; the bridge meter has 50 Ω resistance.

interactives.title: Charging capacitors and growing currents
interactives.sub: Throw the switch on an RC or RL circuit, time the charge to 63%, find the half-life and see why τ = RC.
interactives.note: Exact exponential solutions with ideal components; the clock is sped up or slowed so each time constant is watchable.

interactives.title: Electric fields and potential
interactives.sub: Drag charges and a test charge: field lines, equipotentials, dipoles, null points and the uniform field between plates.
interactives.note: Point charges in a plane, in a vacuum, added by Coulomb's law; field lines are traced numerically.

interactives.title: Charged particles in magnetic fields
interactives.sub: Protons, electrons and alpha particles circling in B, drifting in crossed fields, and a velocity selector to tune.
interactives.note: Uniform fields, non-relativistic speeds; integrated with the Boris method, which keeps the speed exact in a pure magnetic field.

interactives.title: Kinetic theory of gases
interactives.sub: Hundreds of molecules in a box: pressure from wall collisions, Boyle's and Charles's laws, and the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution.
interactives.note: A two-dimensional gas of hard discs with elastic collisions, in units where k = m = 1.

interactives.title: The photoelectric effect
interactives.sub: Shine light on seven metals: thresholds, stopping voltages, intensity against frequency, and Planck's constant from your own data.
interactives.note: Real work functions; the current scale is arbitrary and electron energies are spread evenly up to the maximum.

interactives.title: Radioactive decay and half-life
interactives.sub: Watch individual nuclei decay at random, measure the half-life, and follow a parent–daughter decay chain.
interactives.note: Each nucleus decays independently (Monte Carlo); the dashed curves are the exact equations.

interactives.title: Quantum wells and tunnelling
interactives.sub: Energy levels and wavefunctions in four potentials, solved from the Schrödinger equation, and electrons tunnelling through barriers.
interactives.note: One electron in one dimension; the Schrödinger equation is solved numerically and checked against the exact results.

interactives.title: Time dilation and spacetime
interactives.sub: A light clock on a moving train, length contraction, relativistic velocity addition and a spacetime diagram of simultaneity.
interactives.note: Exact Lorentz transformations for uniform motion; the train is drawn contracted along its motion.

interactives.title: Refraction, lenses and mirrors
interactives.sub: Snell's law and total internal reflection, then ray diagrams for converging and diverging lenses and curved mirrors.
interactives.note: Geometrical optics with thin lenses and paraxial rays; reflected brightness from the Fresnel equations.
